messages.title: How to run it: timeframe, holding time, signal frequency
messages.md:
The author publishes on BTCUSDT 1h. The script's only events are the zero crossings of the smoothed delta (lines 24–25): 1786 over the whole history (2024-11-27 → 2026-11-26), 885 in the last 12 months [[range:2025-11-26T23:00:00Z..2026-11-26T23:00:00Z]], 73.8 per month (run run_4a1c9e02). messages.title: What does the script compute and what signals does it show?
messages.md:
The script splits each bar's volume into buy and sell volume by comparing every realtime tick with the previous close (lines 13–17), accumulating both in `varip` variables that reset on a new bar (lines 6–12). It plots the difference as columns (line 21), its 20-bar SMA as a line (line 22) and a zero level (line 23). Two `alertcondition` calls fire when the smoothed delta crosses zero (lines 24–25); the author presents them as entry (positive) and exit (negative).

| output | line | type | role intended by the author |
|---|---|---|---|
| Delta columns | 21 | columns | visualisation |
| Smoothed line | 22 | line | signal source |
| zero level | 23 | level | threshold |
| Pressure turns positive | 24 | event | entry |
| Pressure turns negative | 25 | event | exit |

messages.title: Which signal is known at bar close and can be placed in an alert?
messages.md:
None. Both alerts (lines 24–25) fire on `smooth`, which is built from `buyVol` and `sellVol` — `varip` accumulators that update on every realtime tick (lines 6–8, 13–17). On a historical bar the script runs once, so the split collapses to the whole bar's volume on one side (line 14: `close >= close[1]`); in realtime it is the tick-by-tick split. The two series differ, so a signal computed on history does not describe what the alert will do, and an alert that fired cannot be checked against the chart afterwards. Example: on [[t:2026-03-22T18:00:00Z@89016]] (the highest-volume bar of the last 12 months, 962) the historical delta is −962 — the whole bar on one side — while any realtime split of the same bar lies between −962 and +962. A close-based reformulation would be a different indicator, not this one. **NO: not tradeable** — blocks B and C are skipped.

| metric | value |
|---|---|
| tradeable signal | none |
| cause | varip accumulators, lines 6–8 and 13–17 |
| alert on history vs. realtime | different series |

messages.title: Does the tradeable signal repaint?
messages.md:
There is no tradeable signal to check. For the author's smoothed delta the truncated-history test (200 points t, run run_b73d10f5) gives identical values on bars ≤ t: on history the script is deterministic. The problem is not repainting but the history/realtime mismatch from `varip` described in A2.

| metric | value |
|---|---|
| signals changed after the fact (history) | 0% |
| code findings | varip (6–8), barstate.isnew (9) |

messages.title: Would the agent put its own $10,000 on this for 6 months?
messages.md:
No. There is nothing to execute: an alert on this script fires on realtime tick data that cannot be reproduced on history, so no backtest describes what the alert would have done.

| metric | value |
|---|---|
| bet | no |

messages.title: What must happen in the forward test for the verdict to change?
messages.md:
Nothing in a forward test can change it: there is no paper journal because there is no rule. The verdict is revisited only if the author publishes a version whose signal is computed from closed bars without `varip`; the cycle then restarts from A1.

|---|---|
| condition for YES | a new version without varip |
